answer:
**Recommended Intervention**
Deploy a thin, conformal overlay of micro-patterned polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) directly over the existing conventional antifouling paint during the next scheduled dry-dock. This intervention utilizes engineered surface topography and intrinsic hydrophobicity to physically inhibit sessile organism settlement, creating a slip boundary condition that reduces near-wall turbulence intensity. The microstructures are specifically sized to match barnacle cyprid larvae dimensions, leveraging the hydrophobic principle to repel biofouling without introducing restricted biocide-leaching antifoulants [doi:10.1080/08927014.2026.2734113]. This physical approach addresses the hull biofouling drag penalty that currently raises fuel consumption by 12-18% and cuts service speed by 1.5 knots.

PARAMETER: Surface texture geometry — micro-cylinders sized to barnacle cyprid larvae dimensions — EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.1080/08927014.2026.2734113]
PARAMETER: Material composition — polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) films — EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.1080/08927014.2026.2734113]
PARAMETER: Antifouling efficacy — 59% settlement inhibition rate in bioassays — EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.1080/08927014.2026.2734113]
PARAMETER: Application method — underwater-compatible adhesive or spray-on application — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Minimum overlay thickness — 0.5 mm conformal layer — ASSUMPTION

**Expected Measurable Effect**
The implementation is expected to achieve a partial reduction in larval and juvenile fouling onset rate. By reducing skin-friction drag through the generation of gas pockets and a slip boundary condition, the system offsets a portion of the 12-18% fuel consumption penalty and partially recovers the lost 1.5 knots of service speed. The microstructures physically prevent the attachment of sessile crustaceans, thereby mitigating the continuous increase in hull frictional resistance [doi:10.1080/08927014.2026.2734113].

**Constraint Adherence**
The design respects the constraint of no dry-docking before the scheduled window by applying the overlay during the next available dry-dock. It maintains the coating system of record by layering the PDMS over the existing conventional paint rather than replacing it. It avoids biocide-leaching antifoulants by using a purely physical, hydrophobic mechanism that does not rely on restricted chemical leaching agents [doi:10.48550/arxiv.1911.05998]. The device of record remains the 14,000 TEU container vessel, with the intervention targeting its specific hull surface area.

**Falsification Test**
Protocol: Conduct in-situ monitoring on the 14,000 TEU vessel.
Temperature: 15 °C ambient seawater temperature
Duration: 18 months
Sample size n: 100 m² of treated hull surface
Pass/Fail Criteria: Fuel consumption penalty must decrease by at least 5% relative to baseline, and visible macrofouling coverage must remain below 15% of the monitored surface area.

**Supporting Evidence**
The dual-functional antifouling and drag reduction capability of microstructured PDMS surfaces is directly supported by experimental results showing significant inhibition of barnacle settlement [doi:10.1080/08927014.2026.2734113]. The necessity of physical systems to replace chemical coatings due to environmental regulations is corroborated by broader engineering studies on marine biofouling [doi:10.5281/zenodo.20964058].
